ideas.body: Mira’s colleague privately told her about an upcoming resignation. Mira was discreet and did not repeat the information to anyone else. Which phrase is closest in meaning to “discreet” as used here?

During a confidential schedule change, Nila checked her notices for accuracy and kept them brief. She was discreet when she withheld the unpublished detail, but later carelessly posted it in a public group. Which phrase expresses the antonym of “discreet” as used here?

A catalogue describes a seal as "authentic" when it is the real seal claimed by its label, rather than a copy. A second seal was made to pass as the seal described on its label, although it was not that seal. Which word is the best antonym of "authentic" in this context?

A reviewer says an outage could have been stopped by activating an available, working backup switch, and therefore rejects the report's description of it as "inevitable". Which word best expresses the antonym of "inevitable" in this context?
A dealer labels a vase as an original. After examining it, an appraiser concludes that it is authentic, not a copy. Which option is closest in meaning to "authentic" as used here?

Choose the word closest in meaning to "transient" as used in the sentence below.
The organisers described the mobile exhibition as transient: it occupied the foyer for one weekend and was then removed as scheduled.

The archive assignment would take several hours and require checking many entries. Rina nevertheless requested it, saying she wanted to do it and needed no encouragement. Which phrase is the clearest antonym of "reluctant" in this context?

At a community arts centre, Arjun teaches music, repairs equipment, and manages bookings. The centre describes him as "versatile" because he takes on these different duties. Which phrase is the antonym of "versatile" in this context?

Choose the option closest in meaning to "prudent" in the sentence below.
Before approving the proposal, the treasurer took a prudent approach, weighing possible risks carefully.

Although Leena was resolute in carrying out her plan, she had been prudent in choosing it: she considered her options and avoided unnecessary risks. Which phrase is opposite in meaning to "prudent" as used here?
Choose the phrase closest in meaning to "benevolent".

During a night watch, Leena looked up from her notes at intervals and spotted a warning sign. She was praised as "vigilant", although she had not checked every detail of the log. Which phrase is the clearest antonym of "vigilant" in this context?

Read the sentence and choose the phrase closest in meaning to “ambiguous” as used here.
After reading the line “They saw her duck,” one classmate said it meant that they watched her lower her head; another said it meant that they saw the bird belonging to her. The teacher described the line as ambiguous.
A caterer prepares only the quantity of food needed for a meal, and its use of food is described as “frugal”. Which phrase expresses an antonym of “frugal” in this context?

Although hired as an illustrator, Nila also edits captions, prepares layouts and presents design ideas to clients. Her manager describes her as versatile. Which phrase is closest in meaning to "versatile" as used here?

Mira had accepted the invitation to present the report, but when her turn came she kept postponing it and hoped a colleague would begin first. Mira was reluctant to present. Which word is closest in meaning to "reluctant" as used here?

Read the sentence and choose the phrase closest in meaning to “inevitable” as used here.
The village’s only road crossed a bridge that was closed for the day, and no alternative route was available. The delivery could not reach the village that day; a delay was inevitable.

At a wildlife reserve, Sana kept watching the river level and the bank for signs that rising water might endanger the camp. Her team described her as “vigilant”. Which phrase is closest in meaning to “vigilant” as used here?

During a debate, the moderator listened closely to both teams and applied the same speaking-time rule to each, without favouring either team. The report described the moderator as "impartial". Which phrase expresses the opposite of "impartial" as used here?
Although the report contains accurate information, its sections are not arranged logically and its explanation is hard to understand. Which word is the best antonym of “coherent” in this context?

A verified log records a power interruption at the exact time of a shutdown. The proposed explanation is that the interruption caused the shutdown; assume the log is reliable evidence supporting this explanation, but not conclusive proof. Choose the sentence in which "plausible" is used to describe an explanation that is reasonable and likely to be true.

After hearing that most colleagues supported the proposal, Devika told the group that she thought its evidence was weak and explained her reasons. The chair described her response as “candid”. Which phrase is closest in meaning to “candid” as used here?

Two reviewers considered an explanation for a late delivery. One found its wording ambiguous, and another remained sceptical; the lead reviewer called it plausible. Which phrase gives the closest meaning of "plausible" as used here?

Read the sentence and choose the option closest in meaning to "sparse" as used here.
Across the vast reserve, settlements were sparse: the survey found only a few villages, with long stretches of open land between them.
Choose the word closest in meaning to "arrogant".

At the end of a long review, the chair asked for a concise report that preserved the decision, the assigned action and the deadline, but left out repeated background. Which phrase is closest in meaning to "concise" as used here?

A report claims that a ferry will arrive by noon. Priya asks questions about the forecast, but she is described as “sceptical” because she doubts that the claim is true. Later, she accepts the claim as true. Which word best expresses an attitude opposite to her initial attitude?

The supplier predicted that its new system would halve a shop’s energy use. Mira asked for evidence before accepting the prediction and remained “sceptical”. Which word is closest in meaning to “sceptical” as used here?
Choose the word that means "not supporting one person or group more than another".

In a review of a report, a student writes: “Each paragraph followed logically from the previous one, and the evidence led clearly to the conclusion. The report was coherent.” Which phrase is closest in meaning to “coherent” as used here?
The excitement proved transient: it faded before the meeting ended, whereas the committee’s resolve continued through months of setbacks. Which word is the best antonym of "transient" as used here?

Choose the word closest in meaning to "conspicuous" in the sentence below.
Though the room was decorated in muted colours, the large gold clock above the doorway remained conspicuous.

At a design review, Meera presented her work confidently. She was described as “arrogant” because she claimed the team’s success as solely hers and dismissed her colleagues’ concerns. Which phrase best expresses an antonym of “arrogant” as used here?

At a review meeting, Mira is asked for her view of a proposal. She openly and honestly says that she opposes it. A second reviewer privately also opposes it but deliberately gives a vague reply so the group will not learn her actual view. Which phrase describes the second reviewer’s response as an antonym of “candid”?

In a planning meeting, Dev clearly stated the outcome he wanted and explained his recommendation with confidence so that the group would take his view seriously. A colleague described Dev as “assertive”. Which phrase is closest in meaning to “assertive” as used here?
In the sentence, "Mira was diligent in carrying out her assigned duties," which phrase is closest in meaning to "diligent"?

A relief group is called "benevolent" because it treats recipients kindly, gives them practical help and offers generous support. Which phrase is the antonym of "benevolent" in this context, reversing all three qualities?

The dictionary definition supplied for this item describes "sparse" as "only present in small amounts or numbers and often spread over a large area." Consider only spatial distribution, not the number of stations. A set of stations spread over a large zone is redesigned so that the stations are packed closely together within a small part of that zone. Which adjective best expresses the spatial opposite of "sparse"?

An editor prepares two notices. Both are logical and well organised, prepared with equal care, and equally easy to see. The first gives only the information that is necessary and important, using few words. The second adds repeated wording and nonessential details. Which word names the first notice’s quality of giving only necessary and important information in few words, a quality the second lacks?
A family was described as frugal after carefully limiting its grocery spending to the amount needed. Which word is closest in meaning to “frugal” in this sentence?
While reviewing an inventory, Sana checked each record and paid close attention to its details. Her supervisor described her work as “meticulous”. Which phrase is closest in meaning to “meticulous”?

Before submitting the ledger, Mira checked each entry against the receipts and corrected every error. Her supervisor described her approach as “conscientious”. Which phrase is closest in meaning to “conscientious” as used here?

Choose the word closest in meaning to “tedious” as used in the sentence below.
Entering the same names into column after column took most of the afternoon. By the end, the volunteers were finding it hard to stay interested, and they described the task as tedious.

At a committee meeting, Dev states his preferred timetable firmly and confidently, and the members take notice. Isha says openly and honestly that she has not formed a preference and is not ready to recommend one. Which phrase best expresses the antonym of "assertive" in this context?

When asked why the parcel arrived late, Nikhil gave an explanation consistent with the dispatch log, which recorded that it had left the warehouse a day late. His explanation was described as "plausible". Which phrase is closest in meaning to "plausible" as used here?

After a sudden closure of her small business, Meera regained her confidence and returned to work soon. Her colleagues described her as "resilient". Which phrase is closest in meaning to "resilient" as used here?

On a museum visit, Leena asks how fossils form, why different materials are used in the exhibits, and what questions researchers are investigating. Her guide describes her as “inquisitive”. Which word is closest in meaning to “inquisitive” in this context?

At the residents’ club, Nisha willingly joins group meals and social activities and rarely chooses to spend her leisure time alone. Her friends describe her as “gregarious”. Which phrase is closest in meaning to “gregarious” as used here?
Which word is closest in meaning to "hostile"?

At a museum, Asha asked questions about exhibits in several unrelated sections. Dev completed the task for one display, declined the optional sections and said he did not want to learn about anything else there. Which word best describes Dev’s attitude as the opposite of Asha’s inquisitive attitude?
At a public event, volunteers wore conspicuous badges so visitors could spot them quickly. Which word is the best antonym of "conspicuous" as used here?

On dissolution, all the firm’s assets have been realised in cash for ₹6,70,000. The firm owes ₹3,20,000 to outside creditors. After those creditors are paid, the only partner advances due are loans of ₹1,20,000 to P and ₹80,000 to Q. Capital claims are ₹1,20,000 for P and ₹1,80,000 for Q, and P and Q share profits equally. There are no other liabilities, realisation expenses, assets, or partner contributions. How much should P receive in total against the partner loan and capital?

A firm is being dissolved. Its firm liabilities exceed its firm assets. Partner R has private debts and private property. Which statement correctly describes the application of R’s private property under the settlement rules?

At the start of a year, A and B carry on a business as a firm. On 1 April, C is admitted and the business continues without the firm closing. On 1 October, B retires and A and C continue the same business; the firm remains open. No assets are realised, liabilities settled or books closed on either date. On 31 March, A and C discontinue the business altogether, realise all the firm’s assets, pay all its liabilities, settle the accounts and close the books. Which option correctly classifies the admission, retirement and final closure?

On dissolution, A and B share profits and losses in the ratio 3:2. Immediately before recording the result of realisation, their capital accounts show credit balances of ₹2,60,000 and ₹2,00,000, respectively. The firm has non-cash assets with a book value of ₹5,00,000 and bank balance of ₹80,000; its only external liability is ₹1,20,000. All the non-cash assets are realised for ₹4,20,000, the liability is settled for ₹1,15,000, and realisation expenses of ₹10,000 are paid. There are no other assets, liabilities, expenses, reserves, partner loans, or capital movements. What amount should be paid to B on final settlement?

On dissolution, a firm has ₹4,20,000 cash available from realised assets. It owes ₹1,20,000 to outside creditors, ₹2,80,000 as a partner loan to K and ₹1,20,000 as a partner loan to M. These are the only amounts payable, and there are no unpaid realisation expenses or partner contributions. Outside creditors are paid before partner loans, and the remaining cash is insufficient to pay both partner loans in full. How much should be paid to M against his partner loan?
Which statement correctly describes the relationship between dissolution of a firm and dissolution of the partnership?

ideas.body:
Arrange the following statements in logical order, beginning with why a company obtains capital from several persons and ending with how their contributions are represented in its accounts.
(A) The contributions are combined in a common account called Share Capital Account.
(B) Since it cannot generate its own capital, the company obtains capital from several persons.
(C) The contributors are shareholders, and their contributions are share capital.
(D) Because shareholders are numerous, a separate capital account is not opened for each.
Choose the correct sequence.

A company has forfeited 500 shares. It subsequently reissues 200 of those shares, while the other 300 remain unreissued. Consider the following statements about the reissue:
(A) Capital profit transferred to Capital Reserve can relate only to the shares reissued.
(B) Any discount allowed on reissue is debited to Share Forfeiture Account.
(C) The entire balance of Share Forfeiture Account for all 500 shares may be transferred to Capital Reserve after only 200 shares are reissued.
(D) Forfeited shares may be reissued only at par.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company has ₹2,00,000 of uncalled capital, of which ₹50,000 is designated as Reserve Capital. The company is not being wound up and needs funds for its normal operations. Which statement applies to the ₹50,000?

A company receives applications for more shares than it offered. Match each description of the directors’ approach or the accounting perspective with the corresponding statement.

List-I
(A) Some applications are accepted in full and the others are rejected
(B) A pro-rata allotment is made to all applicants
(C) The directors combine the two approaches described in (A) and (B)
(D) Accounting perspective on when and within which process over-subscription is resolved

List-II
(I) Shares are allotted to all applicants proportionately
(II) Full acceptance and rejection are used together with pro-rata allotment
(III) It is resolved with allotment and considered within the application-and-allotment process
(IV) Selected applications are accepted in full, and the others are rejected

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company has received ₹2,40,000 as calls in advance. Subsequently, calls of ₹80,000 and ₹95,000 become due, and the full amount of each call is adjusted against the advance. No other advance is received or adjusted. What is the balance in Calls in Advance Account immediately after these adjustments? Ignore interest.

Consider the following statements about collecting the amount on shares:
(A) The first instalment collected with the application is called application money.
(B) The second instalment, collected on allotment, is called allotment money.
(C) Any remaining instalments are termed calls on shares.
(D) A company is required to collect the amount on shares in at least three instalments.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

The company calls ₹6 per allotted share and receives ₹48,600 in total against this call. No other amount has been called or received. Arrange the following capital amounts from largest to smallest:
(I) Authorised capital
(II) Issued capital
(III) Subscribed capital
(IV) Called-up capital
(V) Paid-up capital
(VI) Uncalled capital

Calls in advance of ₹72,000 have already been received and are available in full to adjust against this call. The remaining call money is received in full in cash on the due date, with no other receipts or deductions. How much cash does the company receive on the due date?

A company forfeits 100 shares of ₹10 each, issued at par. The full ₹10 per share has been called up. Each shareholder paid ₹3 per share on application but did not pay the ₹2 per share allotment money or the ₹5 per share call money. No other amount is unpaid.

List-I

(D) Share Calls A/c (Cr.)

List-II

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

At the reporting date, a company has received ₹4,80,000 as calls in advance. Before that date, ₹1,80,000 of this amount was adjusted when the related call became due. The company also received a further ₹90,000 in advance for a call not yet due. No other receipts or adjustments affect the Calls in Advance Account. What balance should be shown under current liabilities as Calls in Advance?

A company validly forfeits shares issued at a premium after a shareholder fails to pay a call. The full share premium had already been received and recorded before forfeiture, and no share premium is outstanding. What is the treatment of the recorded share-premium entry?
A company invites applications for 2,00,000 shares and receives applications for 1,90,000 shares. Which subscription condition is indicated?

A company issues shares for cash and collects the amount in four separate instalments: application money, allotment money, a first call and a final call. The calls are made successively, with the first call preceding the final call. Arrange the instalments in chronological order.
(A) Application money
(B) Allotment money
(C) First call money
(D) Final call money
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company purchases a business from a vendor and settles the entire purchase price by issuing fully paid shares to that vendor. No cash is paid to the vendor. In the same period, the company receives application money in cash from public applicants for a separate share issue. How should the shares issued to the vendor be classified?

A company receives cash from shareholders towards a call that has not yet been made. The amount is specifically paid in advance and is not currently due. Which statements are correct?

(I) The amount received is called Calls in Advance.
(II) The amount is a liability of the company.
(III) The amount is credited directly to Share Capital Account upon receipt.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company receives calls in advance from shareholders. Match each situation in List-I with the accounting treatment in List-II. Assume no other transaction affects these balances.

List-I
(A) A shareholder pays an amount before the related call is due.
(B) The related call becomes due, and the available advance is adjusted against it.
(C) At the balance-sheet date, the related call is not yet due and the advance remains unadjusted.
(D) Interest on the advance is paid through the bank; assume the Articles provide for this interest.

List-II
(I) Calls in Advance A/c Dr.; To Particular Call A/c.
(II) Show the balance separately under current liabilities—other current liabilities; exclude it from paid-up capital.
(III) Bank A/c Dr.; To Calls in Advance A/c.
(IV) Interest on Calls in Advance A/c Dr.; To Bank A/c.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Shares were issued at a premium. The stated shares in each case are forfeited for non-payment of call money. Match each case with the amount to be debited to Securities Premium Reserve Account at forfeiture. All amounts are in rupees.

List-I
(A) 400 shares; premium of ₹6 per share fully received
(B) 300 shares; premium of ₹5 per share wholly unpaid
(C) 250 shares; premium of ₹8 per share, of which ₹4 per share remains unpaid
(D) 200 shares; premium of ₹7 per share, of which ₹3 per share remains unpaid

List-II
(I) ₹0
(II) ₹600
(III) ₹1,000
(IV) ₹1,500

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company has received an amount from a shareholder before the relevant call is made. The amount remains unadjusted until that call becomes due. Match each event or question in List-I with the corresponding treatment in List-II.

List-I
(A) Receipt of the amount before the call is made
(B) Adjustment of the advance when the relevant call becomes due
(C) Balance-sheet presentation of the unadjusted amount
(D) Treatment of the amount in determining paid-up capital

List-II
(I) Show separately under Equity and Liabilities, under current liabilities, as ‘others current liabilities’
(II) Debit Bank A/c and credit Calls in Advance A/c
(III) Do not add the amount to paid-up capital
(IV) Debit Calls in Advance A/c and credit the Particular Call A/c

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) Authorised capital
(B) Issued capital
(C) Subscribed capital
(D) Called-up capital

List-II
(I) The amount of share capital a company is authorised to issue by its Memorandum of Association
(II) The part of authorised capital actually issued to the public for subscription, including shares allotted to vendors and signatories to the company’s memorandum
(III) The part of issued capital actually subscribed by the public

ideas.body: A company issues 800 debentures of nominal value ₹100 each for ₹112 each, 500 debentures of nominal value ₹200 each for ₹218 each, and 300 debentures of nominal value ₹500 each for ₹506 each. All the debentures are issued for the stated prices, and there are no other adjustments. Which option correctly states the total premium on issue and its balance sheet presentation?

A company issues debentures with a nominal value of ₹1,000 each, receives ₹900 per debenture at issue, and undertakes to repay ₹1,100 per debenture on maturity. For this question, an issue proceeds amount below nominal value is an issue at a discount, and a repayment amount above nominal value is redemption at a premium.

(A) The debentures are issued at a discount and redeemable at a premium.
(B) Issue at a discount and redemption at a premium is one of the six situations commonly found in practice.
(C) Because the debentures are issued at a discount, they must be redeemed at par.
(D) Because the debentures are redeemable at a premium, they must have been issued at a premium.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

Match List-I with List-II using the terms defined here: an issue price equal to nominal value is at par, above nominal value is at a premium, and below nominal value is at a discount. A redemption amount equal to nominal value is redeemable at par; an amount above nominal value is redeemable at a premium. All amounts are per debenture.

List-I
(A) Nominal value ₹1,000; issue price ₹1,000; redemption amount ₹1,000
(B) Nominal value ₹1,000; issue price ₹1,100; redemption amount ₹1,000

(II) Issued at a discount and redeemable at a premium
(III) Issued at par and redeemable at a premium
(IV) Issued at a premium and redeemable at par

(A) Assess current profitability and operational efficiency to judge the firm’s financial health.

ideas.body:
A company presents its balance-sheet figures for two periods side by side. It used the same accounting principles in both periods. Consider the following statements:
(A) The figures meet the stated condition for being comparative data.
(B) Expressing each item as a percentage of a common item is the defining basis of a comparative statement.
(C) If different accounting principles are used in two periods, the deviation should be mentioned in a footnote.
(D) The comparison of figures for different periods is called vertical analysis.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

An analyst is reviewing the following features of common-size statements. Which combination of statements is correct?
(A) Each item in a common-size statement is expressed as a percentage of a common item.
(B) Common-size analysis is also known as horizontal analysis.
(C) Common-size statements can be used to compare the operating and financing characteristics of two companies of different sizes in the same industry.
(D) Common-size statements are useful for inter-firm comparisons but not for comparing different years within one firm.

A company reports the following figures: total assets are ₹24 lakh in Year 1 and ₹15 lakh in Year 2; inventories are ₹5 lakh in Year 1 and ₹4 lakh in Year 2. What percentage of total assets is represented by Year 1 inventories in a common-size balance sheet? Give your answer to two decimal places.

Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) A firm presents its balance sheet and statement of profit and loss in comparative form for two periods; the figures indicate trends and direction.
(B) An analyst compares the operating and financing characteristics of two differently sized companies in the same industry using common-base percentages.
(C) The accounting principles used in statements being compared differ, and the departure is disclosed in a footnote.
(D) The analysis that expresses each financial statement item as a percentage of a common item is given a particular name.

List-II
(I) Common size statements facilitate comparison of operating and financing characteristics of differently sized companies in the same industry.
(II) Comparative statements show financial position or profitability for different periods, and their figures indicate trends and direction.
(III) Comparative figures require the same accounting principles; departures are mentioned in a footnote.
(IV) Common size analysis is also known as vertical analysis.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
Company P and Company Q have total assets of ₹10,00,000 and ₹5,00,000, respectively. Inventory is 20% of total assets in each company’s common-size balance sheet. Which interpretation is correct?

Consider the following statements about common-size statements:
(A) In a common-size balance sheet, liabilities are expressed as a percentage of total assets.
(B) A common-size statement prepared for successive periods can show changes in the respective percentages over time.
(C) Common-size analysis can help compare enterprises that differ substantially in size by providing insight into the structure of their financial statements.
(D) In a common-size statement of profit and loss, expenditure items are expressed as a percentage of total assets.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Which statements correctly describe comparative statements?
(A) They show a firm’s profitability and financial position for different periods in comparative form.
(B) The financial data are comparative only when the same accounting principles are used to prepare the statements.
(C) If accounting principles differ, the deviation should be mentioned in a footnote.
(D) Comparative analysis is also known as vertical analysis.

A firm presents its balance sheet and statement of profit and loss for two periods in comparative form. It uses the same accounting principles in both periods. Which of the following statements are correct?
(A) The comparative figures can indicate the trend and direction of the firm’s financial position and operating results.
(B) Financial data can be comparative even when different accounting principles are used and the difference is not disclosed in a footnote.
(C) The data meet the same-accounting-principles condition for being comparative.
(D) This analysis is also known as vertical analysis.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Consider the following statements about the bases used in common-size statements:
(A) In a common-size balance sheet, each asset is expressed as a percentage of total assets.
(B) In a common-size statement of profit and loss, expenditure items are expressed as a percentage of revenue from operations.
(C) In a common-size balance sheet, each asset is expressed as a percentage of revenue from operations.
(D) In a common-size statement of profit and loss, expenditure items are expressed as a percentage of total assets.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
A firm presents its balance sheets for two periods in comparative form. It applied one accounting principle differently in the two periods. What should it do about this difference?

A company presents financial statements for two periods in comparative form. It applied different accounting principles in the two periods and has not disclosed this difference. Consider the following statements:
(A) The financial data are comparative despite the difference in accounting principles.
(B) The deviation in accounting principles should be mentioned in a footnote.
(C) Financial data are comparative only when the same accounting principles are used.
(D) A footnote makes the accounting principles used in the two periods the same.
Choose the correct answer:

A company is preparing a common-size balance sheet and a common-size statement of profit and loss. Consider the following statements about the percentage bases to use:
(A) Inventory in the balance sheet is expressed as a percentage of total assets.
(B) Each liability item in the balance sheet is expressed as a percentage of total liabilities.
(C) An expenditure item in the statement of profit and loss is expressed as a percentage of total assets.
(D) An expenditure item in the statement of profit and loss is expressed as a percentage of total liabilities.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

An analyst is preparing a common-size statement of profit and loss for each year to compare the expenditure structure of two firms of different sizes. The figures are:
Firm A — Year 1: revenue from operations ₹10,00,000; total expenditure ₹8,00,000. Year 2: revenue from operations ₹16,00,000; total expenditure ₹12,00,000.
Firm B — Year 1: revenue from operations ₹20,00,000; total expenditure ₹14,00,000. Year 2: revenue from operations ₹24,00,000; total expenditure ₹18,00,000.
Using each year's revenue from operations as the base for that year's expenditure percentage, which conclusion is correct?

Company P: Year 1—total assets ₹8,00,000, inventories ₹1,60,000, cash and cash equivalents ₹80,000; Year 2—total assets ₹10,00,000, inventories ₹2,00,000, cash and cash equivalents ₹1,00,000.

A company’s financial analyst compares its inventory turnover ratios for two successive accounting periods. The reported figures are:
Year 1: Revenue from operations ₹14,40,000; gross profit ₹3,60,000; opening inventory ₹2,40,000; closing inventory ₹3,60,000.
Year 2: Revenue from operations ₹16,80,000; gross profit ₹4,80,000; opening inventory ₹3,60,000; closing inventory ₹4,40,000.
Which comparison correctly states the inventory turnover ratio for each year? Round each ratio to one decimal place.

For a 365-day accounting period, a firm’s trade payables comprise only creditors and bills payable. At the beginning of the period, creditors were ₹70,000 and bills payable were ₹30,000. At the end, creditors were ₹90,000 and bills payable were ₹50,000. Net purchases for the period were ₹6,00,000; no separate credit-purchase figure is provided. Use the arithmetic mean of beginning and ending trade payables. What was the firm’s average payment period, rounded to the nearest whole day?

A firm's trade payables turnover ratio for the year is 3 times. For its calculation, use annual numerator ÷ average trade payables; the annual numerator is ₹12,75,000. Creditors at the beginning of the year were ₹1,75,000, bills payable at the beginning were ₹1,15,000, and creditors at the end were ₹3,60,000. Average trade payables is one-half of the sum of beginning creditors, beginning bills payable, ending creditors and ending bills payable. What were bills payable at the end of the year?

During the accounting year, Nayan Ltd. reports a high inventory turnover ratio. Its records identify selling inventory rapidly at a low margin to realise cash as the reason for the high ratio; they also show that inventory was not bought in small lots and that there was no obsolete inventory. The finance manager concludes that the high ratio by itself proves improved profitability. Which assessment is best supported?

(A) At a turnover ratio of 5 times, the average collection period is 73 days.
(B) At a turnover ratio of 10 times, the average collection period is 36.5 days.

A company incurs a non-recurring cash outflow associated with a flood loss. The activity from which the outflow arises is not specified.
Which statements correctly describe the outflow and its treatment?
(A) The cash flow should be classified and disclosed separately as arising from the relevant operating, investing or financing activity.
(B) Separate disclosure helps users understand the nature of the item and its effect on present and future cash flows.
(C) The outflow must be classified as an investing activity because it is associated with a flood loss.
(D) A flood loss is an example of an extraordinary item.

A company records the following cash transactions during one accounting period: it receives ₹2,40,000 from the sale of machinery, collects ₹1,10,000 from trade receivables, pays ₹1,80,000 in cash to purchase machinery, pays ₹70,000 to employees, and pays ₹90,000 to purchase marketable securities that constitute cash equivalents. These are the only transactions considered. What is the net cash inflow from these transactions to be reflected in the cash flow statement?

A company has calculated the aggregate net cash flow (or use) from its operating, investing and financing activities for an accounting period. Which expression gives its cash and cash equivalents at the end of the period?

A flood caused a non-recurring loss at Nira Ltd.; for this question, the flood event is treated as an extraordinary item. The company’s only cash outflows directly arising from the flood were ₹2,40,000 for disposal of flood-damaged inventory and site clean-up, ₹1,35,000 for emergency repairs, and ₹75,000 for temporary storage. It also received ₹90,000 insurance compensation for the same event and paid ₹50,000 for routine maintenance unrelated to the flood. What total gross cash outflow arising from the extraordinary event should be calculated for separate disclosure? Do not offset receipts or include unrelated payments.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
A comprehensive plan is being prepared to accomplish an organisation’s objectives. Which set correctly identifies its three dimensions?

A business is formulating a comprehensive plan. It has determined its long-term objective, adopted a course of action and considered the business environment. However, it has not decided what resources are necessary to achieve the objective. Which dimension of the comprehensive plan remains incomplete?

Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) The role of objectives in planning
(B) The future position management seeks to reach
(C) The required quantitative expression of objectives
(D) The period attached to a statement of desired results

(A) The business environment needs to be considered while formulating the strategy.
(B) Changes in the economic, political, social, legal and technological environment affect the organisation’s strategy.
(C) Considering the business environment replaces the need to determine long-term objectives and allocate resources.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A company is organising its work through four separate decisions. Match each decision in List-I with the corresponding step in the organising process in List-II.
List-I
(A) Before deciding departments or job-holders, management breaks the total workload into identifiable activities.
(B) Activities with related features are grouped into departments, without yet naming the employees who will perform them.
(C) After the departments have been settled, specified duties are allotted to particular employees.
(D) For each position, the direct superior to whom its holder reports is recorded.
List-II
(I) Identification and division of work
(II) Departmentalisation
(III) Assignment of Duties
(IV) Establishing reporting relationships
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Arrange the following statements in the causal order in which a functional structure promotes efficiency in the utilisation of manpower, starting with its design feature.
(A) Employees perform similar tasks within a department and are able to improve performance.
(B) Efficiency in the utilisation of manpower is promoted.
(C) Similar or related jobs are grouped together.
(D) Emphasis on specific functions leads to occupational specialisation.
Choose the correct sequence:

A firm is organising a new unit. The teams' tasks are:
Team P: establish reporting relationships
Team Q: assign duties to employees
Team R: identify and divide the work
Team S: group activities into departments
The team labels do not indicate chronological order. Consider the following statements:
(A) Team R's task is the first step in the organising process.
(B) Team Q's task immediately precedes Team P's task.
(C) Team S's task follows Team Q's task.
(D) Team P's task is the final step.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A firm groups its production, finance and marketing employees by function. Employees doing similar tasks coordinate smoothly within each department. However, each functional head prioritises that department’s interests over a stated enterprise-wide objective, and interaction between production and marketing has weakened.
Consider the following statements:
(A) Smooth coordination within departments does not rule out coordination problems between functionally differentiated departments.
(B) Similarity of tasks within a department guarantees that each functional head prioritises enterprise-wide objectives.
(C) Pursuing departmental interests at the expense of organisational interests can hinder interaction between departments.
(D) Smooth coordination within functions necessarily eliminates coordination problems across functions.
Which statements correctly interpret the situation?

A firm groups related jobs into departments according to function. Match each situation in List-I with the corresponding advantage in List-II.
List-I
(A) A new employee’s training is limited to a narrow range of skills used in the assigned function.
(B) A redesign reduces the repeated performance of the same activity by different teams.
(C) The organisational structure gives a place to each of the firm’s different functions.
(D) Employees in one department perform similar tasks.
List-II
(I) Training becomes easier because the focus is on a limited range of skills.
(II) Minimal duplication of effort supports economies of scale and lower cost.
(III) Different functions receive due attention.
(IV) Similar tasks promote control and coordination within a department.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

In a workplace, employees form social ties through interaction and use those ties to communicate about a proposal. Assume the communication uses an informal network rather than a planned route. Arrange the following events in a logically supported sequence, from the origin of the network to its communication outcome.
(A) Employees interact socially.
(B) A network of social relationships arises from their interaction.
(C) Communication takes place through a route that is not planned.
(D) Information spreads faster and feedback is quick.

Match each description in List-I with the delegation element or condition in List-II.

(A) A right derived from formal position to direct a subordinate within the scope of the job

Route B selected 10 employees; 8 met its selection-stage benchmark and 7 met the same on-the-job standard after six months. The employees worked in comparable roles and conditions. For this comparison, effectiveness is measured by the proportion of selected employees who meet the on-the-job standard. Which route has the higher effectiveness on this measure?

A company arranges a classroom away from its actual work floor to recreate a department’s work environment. New employees practise with the same equipment, materials and files they will use in their jobs. Which training method best describes this arrangement?

(A) Human resource personnel search for qualified people to work for the organisation.
(B) Managers throughout the organisation directly deal with and select people to work for it.

(I) Training and development
(II) Recruitment

(IV) Staffing's focus on the human element

A firm’s two units use the same technology and face comparable operating conditions, but the quality of their human resources differs. When assessing their capacity to achieve organisational goals, which principle should guide the assessment?

A business has vacancies and is considering candidates from its existing workforce as well as candidates from outside. It seeks fresh talent and a wider choice of candidates. Consider the following statements:
(A) External sources of recruitment are used to obtain fresh talent and a wider choice.
(B) Recruitment from within the enterprise is internal recruitment.

(II) Contractors can supply the required number of unskilled workers at short notice.
(III) Recruitment from educational institutions for various jobs.
(IV) Applicants introduced by present employees, or their friends and relatives, whose background is sufficiently known.

A company is estimating staffing needs for two units. For Unit X, planned task volume and the number of employees available have both increased. At a small organisation, the line manager is reviewing two career moves: Employee P would receive a new title but no increase in responsibility; Employee Q would be placed in a position of increased responsibility. Consider the following statements about promotions and employee development:

List-II

(D) The increase from 1951 to 1981 was ₹3,574.

Which of the above statements are correct?

The district plans additional public outlays for education and health, with the aim of pursuing economic growth and equity together. Each plan describes where the additional outlays extend services; “only” means that the proposed extension does not reach the other group. Which plan best applies this objective?

A firm employs an educated workforce. Which statements describe contributions of human capital that may be relevant to the firm?
(A) Enhanced human capital can raise labour productivity and stimulate innovation.
(B) An educated workforce can facilitate adaptation to new technologies.
(C) Human capital can raise labour productivity but cannot stimulate innovation.
(D) An educated workforce cannot facilitate adaptation to new technologies.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

An account cites villagers’ use of e-mail as an example of transformation, projects e-governance as a way of the future, and states that the value of IT depends greatly on the existing level of economic development. It raises, without answering, whether IT-based services in rural areas lead to human development. An agency compares two rural areas with different existing levels of economic development. Which conclusion is supported by the stated principle?
A person without formal education is healthy and can provide an uninterrupted labour supply for a longer period. Which conclusion about health and economic growth follows?

A district programme funds medical facilities for two groups of sick labourers who previously lacked access to them. Before access was provided, each of 8 labourers in Group I abstained from work for 3 working days, and each of 5 labourers in Group II abstained for 2 working days. After receiving access, all of them worked those same days. Assume that no other conditions changed and that each resumed working day represents one labour-day of productive work. Which conclusion correctly combines the number of labour-days restored with the human-capital implication of the programme?

A district programme records the following separate, fully spent investments: education ₹2,40,000; health ₹1,20,000; on-the-job training ₹80,000; migration ₹60,000; and information ₹40,000. These five outlays are the programme’s entire expenditure and do not overlap. For this calculation, count education as the main source category and the other four investments as the other source categories. What percentage of the programme’s total expenditure is devoted to the other source categories, rounded to the nearest whole percentage point?

An education investment is introduced. Annual output of goods and services is 4,800 units before the investment and 5,040 units after it. Assume the entire change is attributable to the investment and that the output figures cover comparable periods and use the same units. Using the pre-investment output as the base, calculate the percentage change and identify whether the stated condition for calling the investment unproductive is met.

In a developing economy, human capital (education and health) has grown faster than per-capita real income. Treat these growth rates as the only observations available. Which statement is supported?
(A) The faster human-capital growth caused the slower growth of per-capita real income.
(B) The growth rates alone do not establish a cause-and-effect relation between human-capital growth and economic growth.
(C) The slower growth of per-capita real income establishes that human capital made no contribution to economic growth.
(D) The faster human-capital growth establishes that it raised per-capita real-income growth.

A district programme involves (i) on-the-job training for workers, (ii) investment in health, (iii) migration and (iv) provision of information. Consider the following statements about these measures and human capital formation:
(A) On-the-job training and investment in health are sources of human capital formation.
(B) Migration and information are not sources of human capital formation.
(C) Investment in education is one main source, and health, on-the-job training, migration and information are other sources.
(D) Education is the only source of human capital formation.
Which statements are correct?

Treat “nearly” and “about” as approximate; the 3–6 per cent rate is the reported range for rural and urban areas together. Match List-I with List-II.

(II) Rural female graduates: nearly 11 percentage points higher than rural male graduates

A rural estimate states that more than 10% of farm goods are wasted because of lack of storage. A district produces 7,20,000 kg of farm goods annually, of which 60% comes from farms lacking adequate storage. For this exercise, apply a 10% reference rate to that subgroup’s output solely to calculate a benchmark; this is not an assertion that the actual loss rate is exactly 10%. What benchmark quantity of wastage does the model give?

(A) Credit from the pooled money is given to a needy member.

(II) This demand trend offers organic agriculture a route to generate income through exports.

For this exercise, treat the source shares as exact: inland sources together account for 75% of each cooperative’s total value, and the marine sector accounts for the remaining 25%. Each cooperative divides its inland-source value equally between river-sourced and lake-sourced fish; all marine-sector value is sea-sourced. What are the combined values attributed to river, lake and sea across both cooperatives, respectively?

(D) Work can also help address social issues such as child labour.
